storyTitle: As an IT Support Manager, I want to review ticket performance and SLA reports so that I can measure service delivery against operational targets

functional.title: Generate SLA performance report for a reporting period and verify summary metrics, detailed rows, and data-quality exception count are derived from auditable lifecycle and SLA records
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated and has permission to view and export SLA performance reports for organization scope 'North Region'.

The reporting dataset contains auditable ticket records for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30, including TCK-2048 and TCK-2055 with controlled lifecycle timestamps, assignment history, and persisted SLA metric records.

At least one ticket in the same period has incomplete required lifecycle timestamps for a time-based metric so it should be excluded from aggregate calculations and counted in the visible exception total.
The user is on the support reporting interface and can open the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' area in a supported desktop browser.

steps.action: Open the support reporting interface and click the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' menu option.
steps.expectedResult: The reporting view opens successfully and shows filter controls for Reporting Period, Category, Priority, Status, Assignee, and Organizational Scope.

steps.action: Set Reporting Period to '2026-09-01' through '2026-09-30' and leave all optional filters unset so the report returns the full authorized North Region dataset.
steps.expectedResult: The selected date range is accepted without validation error and the filter state displays the chosen reporting period.

steps.action: Click the 'Run Report' button.
steps.expectedResult: The system queries ticket lifecycle timestamps, assignment history, and SLA metric records, then returns the report without exposing any non-audited source fields.

steps.action: Review the on-screen summary section for the generated report.
steps.expectedResult: Summary metrics are displayed for first response time, resolution time, SLA attainment percentage, backlog aging, and workload trend totals for the selected period.

steps.action: Review the detailed report rows and locate sample tickets TCK-2048 and TCK-2055.
steps.expectedResult: Detailed rows are shown for matching tickets with values consistent with their controlled lifecycle and SLA records, and the rows correspond to the same reporting period.

steps.action: Review the data-quality or exclusion indicator shown with the report output.
steps.expectedResult: A visible excluded-record or exception count is displayed for tickets with incomplete required timestamps, and those excluded tickets are not included in the time-based aggregates.

steps.action: Cross-check one sample metric for TCK-2048 using the underlying auditable ticket history and SLA metric record available in the system.
steps.expectedResult: The report value for the sample ticket matches the approved lifecycle timestamps and persisted SLA metric data, confirming the report uses authoritative sources.

postconditions: A report for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30 is displayed for MGR-04 within the user's authorized organizational scope.
Summary metrics and detailed rows are populated from auditable lifecycle, assignment, and SLA data only.
Tickets with incomplete required timestamps remain excluded from time-based aggregates and are represented in the visible exception count.
Report execution details such as filter payload and row or exclusion counts are available in system observability logs.

functional.title: Apply combined operational filters and verify the returned dataset matches all selected criteria and authorized organizational visibility
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated with permission to view reports only for organization scope 'North Region'.

The reporting dataset for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30 contains tickets across multiple categories, priorities, statuses, assignees, and organization scopes, including tickets assigned to AGENT-12 in category 'Hardware' with priority 'High'.
At least one otherwise similar ticket exists outside North Region or with a non-matching filter attribute so exclusion can be verified.

steps.action: Open the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' view.
steps.expectedResult: The reporting page loads and displays all supported filters.

steps.action: Set Reporting Period to '2026-09-01' through '2026-09-30', Category to 'Hardware', Priority to 'High', Status to 'Resolved', Assignee to 'AGENT-12', and Organizational Scope to 'North Region'.
steps.expectedResult: Each selected filter is accepted as a supported value and appears as the current filter set.

steps.action: Click 'Run Report'.
steps.expectedResult: The system refreshes the report using the full filter combination and returns only records that satisfy all selected conditions.

steps.action: Inspect the detailed rows returned in the report.
steps.expectedResult: Every displayed row matches all selected filters: reporting period within September 2026, category Hardware, priority High, status Resolved, assignee AGENT-12, and organization scope North Region.

steps.action: Verify that a known non-matching record, such as a South Region ticket or a North Region ticket with a different assignee or priority, is not present in the result set.
steps.expectedResult: Records outside the selected organizational scope or with any non-matching filter attribute are excluded from the dataset.

steps.action: Review the summary metrics shown above the grid.
steps.expectedResult: The summary values are recalculated for only the filtered subset and are not based on broader unfiltered data.

steps.action: Change only the Assignee filter from 'AGENT-12' to 'AGENT-17' and rerun the report.
steps.expectedResult: The dataset and summary metrics update to the new operational segment, demonstrating that managers can compare reporting segments by adjusting filters.

postconditions: The report remains displayed with the most recently applied filter set.
Returned data is restricted both by selected filters and by MGR-04's authorized organizational visibility.
Updated report executions for each filter set are captured in observability logs with the applied filter payload.

functional.title: Export the currently displayed filtered report and verify exported rows and summary values exactly match the on-screen report state at time of export
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated and has permission to view and export SLA performance reports.
A filtered report is already generated on screen for Reporting Period '2026-09-01' through '2026-09-30', Priority 'High', and Organizational Scope 'North Region'.
The application supports export in an approved file format such as CSV or XLSX and the test environment allows file download access.
The current on-screen report contains visible summary metrics, detailed rows, and any exclusion count.

steps.action: On the displayed report, note the current filters, the visible summary values, the exception count, and at least two sample row identifiers such as TCK-2048 and TCK-2055 if present.
steps.expectedResult: The exact report state to be exported is clearly identified before export.

steps.action: Click the 'Export' button and choose the supported default export format.
steps.expectedResult: The system starts the export for the currently displayed filtered report without changing the filter state or recalculating against a different dataset.

steps.action: Open the downloaded export file.
steps.expectedResult: The file downloads successfully and opens without corruption in the selected format.

steps.action: Compare the exported report summary section or equivalent summary values with the on-screen summary values captured before export.
steps.expectedResult: Exported summary metrics match the on-screen values exactly for response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, backlog aging, workload trends, and any visible exclusion count if included in the export.

steps.action: Compare the exported detail rows with the on-screen detail grid for the current filter set.
steps.expectedResult: The exported rows contain the same filtered records shown on screen and do not include records outside the displayed dataset.

steps.action: Verify sample records in the export, including ticket IDs and report values for at least two rows.
steps.expectedResult: Sample row values in the export match the on-screen values exactly at the time export was initiated.

steps.action: Review audit or usage logging available to the tester for report export actions.
steps.expectedResult: An export action is recorded with the actor, report identifier, timestamp, and filter context for audit review.

postconditions: A supported export file is generated for the exact filtered report state displayed to the manager.
On-screen report data remains unchanged after export completes.
The export action is recorded in report usage or audit history with the relevant filter context.

functional.title: Verify report access for an authorized manager is limited to the manager's permitted organizational scope even when broader data exists
preconditions: User MGR-09 is authenticated and has report-view permission limited to organizational scope 'Team A' only.
The reporting dataset contains valid records for both Team A and Team B during 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30.
At least one ticket in Team B matches the same category, priority, and status values as a Team A ticket so scope-based restriction can be distinguished from business filters.

steps.action: Open the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' page as MGR-09.
steps.expectedResult: The reporting page opens successfully for the authorized user.

steps.action: Set Reporting Period to '2026-09-01' through '2026-09-30' and select a filter combination known to match records in both Team A and Team B, such as Category 'Hardware' and Status 'Open'.
steps.expectedResult: The filter values are accepted and ready to run.

steps.action: Review the Organizational Scope filter options available to MGR-09.
steps.expectedResult: Only authorized scope values are available to select, or Team A is enforced automatically by the system.

steps.action: Click 'Run Report'.
steps.expectedResult: The report is generated using only the subset of records within MGR-09's authorized Team A visibility.

steps.action: Inspect the detailed rows and compare against known setup data that includes matching Team B records.
steps.expectedResult: Only Team A records are returned; matching Team B records are not visible in the result set.

steps.action: Review the summary metrics for the generated report.
steps.expectedResult: Summary values reflect only Team A data and do not incorporate Team B ticket history or SLA metrics.

postconditions: MGR-09 can use reporting features only within the authorized organizational scope.
No Team B ticket metrics or detailed records are exposed to MGR-09.
The executed report is logged with the actor and constrained scope used for data retrieval.

negative.title: Reject invalid reporting filter combinations and unsupported filter values before report generation
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated and has permission to view SLA performance reports.
The user is on the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' page with empty or default filters.
The UI supports editable Reporting Period, Status, Priority, Category, Assignee, and Organizational Scope fields with validation.

steps.action: Enter a Reporting Period start date of '2026-09-30' and end date of '2026-09-01'.
steps.expectedResult: The date range is flagged as invalid because the start date is after the end date.

steps.action: Attempt to set one or more unsupported filter values, such as a non-enumerated Status or Priority value through the UI or pasted input if the control permits manual entry.
steps.expectedResult: Unsupported enumerations are rejected and a clear validation message is shown; invalid values are not accepted into the active filter set.

steps.action: Enter an assignee value that does not exist in the authorized dataset, such as 'AGENT-99', if the control allows search or free entry.
steps.expectedResult: The system rejects the invalid assignee selection and indicates that the assignee must exist in the authorized dataset.

steps.action: Click the 'Run Report' button with the invalid filter state still present.
steps.expectedResult: The report is not executed, no result set is returned, and the page displays validation feedback identifying the invalid fields.

steps.action: Correct only the date range but leave another invalid filter value unresolved, then click 'Run Report' again.
steps.expectedResult: The system continues to block report execution until all invalid filters are corrected.

steps.action: Clear all invalid values and enter a valid filter set.
steps.expectedResult: Validation errors are removed, confirming the issue was input validation rather than a system failure.

postconditions: No invalid report execution occurs while any filter validation error remains.
No report data, metrics, or exportable dataset is generated from invalid filter input.
The user remains on the reporting page with validation feedback available for correction.

negative.title: Deny unauthorized user access to reporting view and export without exposing ticket metrics or underlying data
preconditions: User EMP-1001 or another authenticated user without reporting permission is available for testing.
The system contains valid SLA performance reporting data for the target period, but the test user has no permission to view or export it.
A direct navigation URL to the reporting page or an export endpoint is available.

steps.action: Log in as EMP-1001 and attempt to navigate directly to the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' page using the menu or direct URL.
steps.expectedResult: Access is denied and the user receives an authorization error or forbidden state instead of the reporting view.

steps.action: Review the denied-access screen or message.
steps.expectedResult: No ticket metrics, summary values, detailed report rows, filter history, or underlying ticket data are displayed.

steps.action: Attempt to call the report export action directly, such as by using an export URL or pressing an export control if present in error.
steps.expectedResult: The export is blocked with an authorization error and no report file is generated.

steps.action: Use browser navigation to retry the unauthorized page or refresh the denied state.
steps.expectedResult: The user remains denied consistently; access is not granted through refresh, back navigation, or deep link retry.

steps.action: Review any observable audit or security log entry available to the tester.
steps.expectedResult: The unauthorized access attempt is recorded for audit or troubleshooting without disclosing protected report content to the user.

postconditions: The unauthorized user cannot view report data or export results.
No sensitive ticket metrics or ticket-level detail is exposed during the denial flow.
Unauthorized report or export attempts are auditable.

negative.title: Handle report execution when tickets with incomplete lifecycle timestamps exist by excluding them from time-based aggregates and surfacing the exception count
preconditions: User MGR-04 is authenticated with permission to view SLA performance reports.

The reporting dataset for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30 includes at least one ticket with missing required lifecycle timestamps for response or resolution calculations, and also includes fully complete tickets in the same filter scope.
The incomplete-ticket records still have enough data to be returned or referenced in the reporting result context but are not valid for time-based aggregation.

steps.action: Open the reporting page and set Reporting Period to '2026-09-01' through '2026-09-30' with filters broad enough to include both complete and incomplete tickets.
steps.expectedResult: The selected period is accepted and the report is ready to run.

steps.action: Click 'Run Report'.
steps.expectedResult: The system completes report generation successfully instead of failing due to incomplete records.

steps.action: Review the summary metrics for first response time and resolution time.
steps.expectedResult: Time-based aggregates are displayed using only tickets with complete required timestamps.

steps.action: Review the visible data-quality exception indicator associated with the report.
steps.expectedResult: The report shows a non-zero excluded-record or incomplete-data count representing tickets omitted from time-based calculations.

steps.action: Compare the aggregate count basis or sample ticket inclusion against known setup data.
steps.expectedResult: Known incomplete tickets are not contributing to response-time or resolution-time averages, but the report clearly communicates their exclusion.

steps.action: Verify the page remains usable for further filter adjustments after the exception is shown.
steps.expectedResult: The report stays available and does not present a generic processing error for this data-quality condition.

postconditions: The report is generated even when incomplete lifecycle records are present.
Incomplete records are excluded only from affected time-based aggregates and counted visibly as data-quality exceptions.
Managers can continue using the report without data corruption or silent metric inflation.

edgeCases.title: Generate report for a valid period where all matching tickets have incomplete lifecycle timestamps and verify exclusion handling
preconditions: User is logged in as IT Support Manager MGR-04 with permission to view and export SLA performance reports for organizational scope 'Infrastructure Support'.
Reporting screen 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' is available and accessible from the support reporting interface.

Test data exists in 'Infrastructure Support' for reporting period 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-07 where 3 tickets match filters Category='Hardware', Priority='High', Status='Closed', Assignee='AGENT-12', but each ticket is missing at least one required controlled lifecycle timestamp needed for response time or resolution time calculation.

Persisted SLA metric records and ticket audit history are available for the same tickets, and the system is configured to exclude incomplete records from time-based aggregates while displaying a visible data-quality exception total.

steps.action: Open the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' area and confirm the page displays report filters for Reporting Period, Category, Priority, Status, Assignee, and Organizational Scope.
steps.expectedResult: The reporting page loads successfully for MGR-04, all expected filters are visible, and no report data is shown until filters are applied or defaults load.

steps.action: Set Reporting Period to '2026-08-01' through '2026-08-07', Category to 'Hardware', Priority to 'High', Status to 'Closed', Assignee to 'AGENT-12', and Organizational Scope to 'Infrastructure Support'.
steps.expectedResult: All selected filter chips/fields display the chosen values exactly and remain in the active filter state.

steps.action: Click the 'Apply' or 'Run Report' button.
steps.expectedResult: The system validates the filter set, executes the report query, and returns a report based only on ticket lifecycle timestamps, assignment history, and auditable SLA metric data for records matching all selected filters.

steps.action: Review the on-screen summary metrics for first response time, resolution time, SLA attainment percentage, backlog aging, and workload trend totals.
steps.expectedResult: Time-based metrics do not include the 3 incomplete tickets in averages or attainment calculations, workload/backlog counts reflect the filtered dataset as defined by the report logic, and the UI clearly indicates that records with incomplete required timestamps were excluded from time-based aggregates.

steps.action: Review the visible data-quality exception area or excluded-record counter on the report.
steps.expectedResult: The report displays an exclusion count of 3 for incomplete lifecycle data, and the exception indication is visible without needing to inspect raw ticket data.

steps.action: Open the detailed rows section for the same filtered result set.
steps.expectedResult: Detailed rows correspond only to tickets matching all filters, and the report presentation does not fabricate response or resolution values for excluded time-based records.

steps.action: Change only the reporting period to another valid range known to contain complete lifecycle records, then rerun the report.
steps.expectedResult: The report refreshes successfully, summary metrics change according to the new filtered dataset, and the exclusion count updates from 3 to the correct value for the new period.

steps.action: Return to the original period '2026-08-01' through '2026-08-07' and rerun the report to verify repeatability.
steps.expectedResult: The same exclusion count of 3 and the same filtered report behavior reappear, demonstrating consistent handling of incomplete lifecycle timestamps.

postconditions: No ticket, assignment, or SLA source data is modified by report generation.
The manager remains on the reporting page with the last applied filters visible.
A report execution log entry is created containing the filter payload, returned row count, and exclusion count for incomplete timestamps.

edgeCases.title: Generate and export a large valid report dataset and verify on-screen summaries reconcile with export output
preconditions: User is logged in as IT Support Manager MGR-04 with permission to view and export SLA performance reports for organizational scopes 'Infrastructure Support' and 'Service Desk East'.

A large test dataset exists for reporting period 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31 containing at least 5,000 tickets with valid controlled lifecycle timestamps, assignment history, and persisted SLA calculation records across multiple categories, priorities, statuses, and assignees within MGR-04's authorized scope.
The reporting application supports export in at least one file format, such as CSV or XLSX, from the current filtered report view.
Expected sampled reconciliation data is known for filter set: Reporting Period='2026-07-01 to 2026-07-31', Priority='High', Status='Resolved', Organizational Scope='Infrastructure Support'.

steps.action: Open 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' and set Reporting Period to '2026-07-01' through '2026-07-31', Priority to 'High', Status to 'Resolved', and Organizational Scope to 'Infrastructure Support'; leave Category and Assignee unselected.
steps.expectedResult: The filter panel accepts the valid range and selected values, showing only supported enumerations and authorized organizational scope values.

steps.action: Click 'Run Report' and wait for the report to render.
steps.expectedResult: The report returns results for the large dataset within acceptable operational response time, without error, and displays summary metrics for response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, backlog aging, and workload trend totals.

steps.action: Capture the displayed summary values and note the total detailed row count shown on screen for the current filter set.
steps.expectedResult: The UI presents stable, readable summary values and a detailed row total for the exact filtered dataset currently displayed.

steps.action: Inspect several detailed rows from the beginning, middle, and end of the result set using pagination or scrolling, and confirm they all match Priority='High', Status='Resolved', and Organizational Scope='Infrastructure Support'.
steps.expectedResult: All sampled rows comply with every selected filter and no out-of-scope records appear in the dataset.

steps.action: Click the 'Export' action and select the supported export format offered by the application.
steps.expectedResult: The export is initiated successfully for the current filtered report and completes without changing the on-screen filters or report content.

steps.action: Open the exported file and verify the exported detailed rows contain the same filtered records and no records outside the selected reporting period, priority, status, or authorized organizational scope.
steps.expectedResult: The exported dataset matches the current on-screen filter context exactly and contains no unauthorized or unfiltered records.

steps.action: Compare the exported file's total row count and sampled summary-related values against the report values captured on screen before export.
steps.expectedResult: The export row count reconciles to the on-screen detailed row count, and the exported summary-related values or derivable totals match the displayed report at the time of export.

steps.action: Return to the application and confirm the report page still shows the same filter chips, same summary values, and same dataset immediately after export.
steps.expectedResult: The report state is preserved after export, enabling management review without rerunning or losing context.

postconditions: An export file is generated for the exact filtered report viewed by MGR-04.
The manager remains authenticated and stays on the reporting screen with filters preserved.
Audit/observability records are created for report execution and export action, including filter payload, row counts, and export event metadata.

accessibility.title: Verify keyboard-only access for applying filters, reviewing results, and exporting the SLA performance report
preconditions: User is logged in as IT Support Manager MGR-04 with permission to view and export SLA performance reports.
Desktop browser is open on the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' page with no mouse use during the test.

Test data exists for reporting period 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-15 with results available for Category='Software', Priority='Medium', Status='Resolved', Assignee='AGENT-17', Organizational Scope='Service Desk East'.

steps.action: Starting from the browser address bar, use Tab and Shift+Tab only to move through the reporting page controls.
steps.expectedResult: Keyboard focus moves in a logical order through the page title region, filter controls, 'Run Report' button, report content area, and 'Export' action, with a visible focus indicator on each interactive element.

steps.action: Use keyboard input to set Reporting Period to '2026-09-01' through '2026-09-15', select Category='Software', Priority='Medium', Status='Resolved', Assignee='AGENT-17', and Organizational Scope='Service Desk East'.
steps.expectedResult: Each filter can be opened, navigated, and selected without a mouse; selected values are announced or visibly updated; no control traps keyboard focus.

steps.action: Tab to the 'Run Report' button and press Enter or Space.
steps.expectedResult: The report runs successfully from keyboard input alone, and focus remains managed predictably without jumping to the browser chrome or an unrelated page area.

steps.action: After results load, use Tab, arrow keys, and any provided keyboard interaction to move through summary cards, detailed rows, pagination controls if present, and the 'Export' action.
steps.expectedResult: All key report interactions are reachable and operable by keyboard, the current focus location is always visible, and the user can review report content without requiring pointer interaction.

steps.action: Activate the 'Export' action using the keyboard and complete any format selection using keyboard controls only.
steps.expectedResult: Export starts successfully through keyboard interaction, and any dialog, menu, or dropdown involved is fully keyboard accessible with visible focus and standard dismissal behavior.

steps.action: After export initiation/completion, continue tabbing through the page and then reverse using Shift+Tab.
steps.expectedResult: Focus order remains logical after export, no hidden or disabled element receives focus unexpectedly, and the user can continue interacting with the report screen.

postconditions: The report can be filtered, executed, and exported using only keyboard input.
No unexpected focus loss, keyboard trap, or inaccessible interactive control is observed on the reporting page.
If export is completed, an export audit entry is created without altering the current report filters or report view.

accessibility.title: Verify screen reader announcements and accessible names for report filters, exception count, summaries, detailed rows, and authorization denial state
preconditions: A supported screen reader is enabled in the test browser.
Two test accounts are available: authorized IT Support Manager MGR-04 with report view/export permission, and unauthorized user AGENT-12 without reporting permission.
Test data exists for period 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-07 where filtered results include visible summary metrics and an exclusion count for incomplete lifecycle timestamps.

steps.action: Log in as MGR-04, open the 'SLA Performance and Overdue Reporting' page, and navigate through the page using screen reader reading commands and Tab navigation.
steps.expectedResult: The page has a meaningful title and landmarks/regions, and each filter control is announced with an accessible name that matches its visual label, such as Reporting Period, Category, Priority, Status, Assignee, and Organizational Scope.

steps.action: Set filters for Reporting Period='2026-08-01 to 2026-08-07' and the prepared dataset, then run the report while listening for screen reader feedback.
steps.expectedResult: The action control is announced clearly, the report refresh is communicated appropriately, and the user can identify when report results are available.

steps.action: Navigate to the summary metrics area and the visible data-quality exception count using the screen reader.
steps.expectedResult: Summary values for response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, backlog aging, and workload trends are announced in a meaningful label-value pattern, and the exclusion/exception total is announced clearly enough for the user to understand that incomplete records were excluded from time-based aggregates.

steps.action: Move through the detailed report rows and any table headers using screen reader table navigation commands.
steps.expectedResult: Column headers and row values are associated correctly, enabling the user to understand each detailed row in context and confirm that the screen content aligns with the report output.

steps.action: Use the screen reader to navigate to and activate the 'Export' control.
steps.expectedResult: The export control has an accessible name that identifies its purpose, and any resulting status message is announced without exposing unrelated or hidden content.

steps.action: Sign out, log in as AGENT-12, and attempt to open the reporting route directly and then attempt export access if any direct URL or control path is available.

postconditions: Authorized users can understand and operate the reporting interface with a screen reader, including filters, summaries, exceptions, detailed rows, and export.

performance.title: Baseline load test for manager SLA performance dashboard with standard reporting period
performance.description: Validate that the reporting view returns summary metrics and detailed rows within acceptable response times for a standard operational workload when authorized IT Support Managers access the dashboard concurrently using common filters such as 30-day reporting period, priority, status, assignee, and organizational scope.
preconditions: Production-like environment is available with monitoring enabled for application, database, cache, and infrastructure layers
Authorized IT Support Manager accounts exist with valid reporting access and organizational scope restrictions
Test dataset contains auditable ticket lifecycle records, assignment history, and persisted SLA metric data for at least 12 months
Standard report response time targets are defined by stakeholders
Observability logs capture execution time, filter payload, row counts, exclusion counts, and export actions

steps.action: Prepare a dataset containing at least 500,000 tickets with associated lifecycle timestamps, assignment audit history, and SLA metric records distributed across categories, priorities, statuses, assignees, and organizational scopes.
steps.expectedResult: Dataset is loaded successfully and represents realistic reporting patterns with valid and incomplete records for exclusion-count calculations.

steps.action: Configure load test scripts for 100 concurrent IT Support Manager users opening the reporting view and applying a standard 30-day date range with common filters.
steps.expectedResult: Load scripts are ready and simulate authenticated, authorized manager behavior only.

steps.action: Run the load for 30 minutes with a steady arrival pattern where users view summary metrics, paginate detailed rows, adjust one filter, and refresh results.
steps.expectedResult: System sustains the workload without functional failures or abnormal latency spikes.

steps.action: Capture P50, P95, and P99 response times for initial report load, filtered report refresh, and pagination requests.
steps.expectedResult: Measured latencies remain within agreed performance targets for standard load.

steps.action: Capture throughput in TPS, application error rate, CPU utilization, memory utilization, database utilization, and cache hit ratio during the run.
steps.expectedResult: Throughput remains stable, error rate stays within acceptable threshold, and resource utilization remains below operational limits.

steps.action: Review report results and verify that summary metrics, detail rows, and exclusion counts are consistently returned during the test.
steps.expectedResult: Responses remain complete and consistent with no partial render, timeout, or data-shape corruption under load.

postconditions: Performance metrics are stored for trend comparison
Any bottlenecks in query execution, aggregation, or rendering are documented
performance.testData: 500,000 tickets; 12 months history; 100 manager users; 30-day filter; mixed categories, priorities, statuses, assignees, org scopes

preconditions: Environment contains at least 50 organizational scopes with realistic ticket distribution
Manager accounts are mapped to authorized scopes
Role-based access and scope filtering are active

steps.action: Prepare scripts for 150 concurrent manager users, each assigned to one or more organizational scopes with valid access.
steps.expectedResult: Scripts represent realistic concurrent access patterns across authorized scopes.

steps.action: Execute a 45-minute load where users open the reporting area and apply combinations of date range, category, priority, status, assignee, and organizational scope filters.
steps.expectedResult: System processes concurrent scope-aware queries successfully.

steps.action: Record P50, P95, and P99 response times for filter validation, report retrieval, and subsequent filter changes.
steps.expectedResult: Latency remains within defined thresholds for the expected concurrent workload.

steps.action: Measure TPS, error rate, CPU, memory, database connections, and query execution times.
steps.expectedResult: Resource consumption remains stable with no pool exhaustion or excessive query contention.

steps.action: Inspect logs to confirm filter payloads and row counts are captured without introducing material latency overhead.
steps.expectedResult: Observability logging works correctly and does not materially degrade performance.

postconditions: Cross-scope concurrency findings are documented
Query hotspots by organizational scope are identified if present
performance.testData: 1,000,000 tickets across 50 org scopes; 150 concurrent users; mixed filter combinations

steps.expectedResult: Script targets worst-case large-range report access patterns.

steps.action: Run the workload for 20 minutes while users request on-screen summaries and page through detailed rows.
steps.expectedResult: System remains responsive under historical high-volume queries.

steps.action: Capture P50, P95, and P99 response times for initial report generation and page retrieval.
steps.expectedResult: Latency is measurable and within approved limits for large-range reports, or breaches are clearly identified.

steps.action: Measure TPS, error rate, CPU, memory, disk I/O, database CPU, temporary space usage, and long-running query counts.
steps.expectedResult: No critical infrastructure saturation or unbounded query growth occurs.

steps.action: Validate that exclusion counts for incomplete lifecycle data are still computed and returned correctly under load.

Capacity recommendations are documented if thresholds are exceeded

performance.title: Load test for rapid filter adjustments and comparative analysis workflow

userStoryObject.title: As an IT Support Manager, I want to review ticket performance and SLA reports so that I can measure service delivery against operational targets
userStoryObject.description:
CONTEXT & BACKGROUND:

IT Support Managers need consistent reporting from ticket lifecycle activity to measure whether the help desk is meeting operational targets. This story supports feature-38 by turning auditable Support Ticket, Assignment, and SLA Metric history into management reporting for response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, backlog aging, and workload trends.

CURRENT STATE:

Reporting is not standardized across ticket lifecycle data, assignment changes, and SLA calculations. Managers must rely on manual extraction or inconsistent interpretations of timestamps and statuses, which creates risk of inaccurate service measurement and weak operational governance.

DESIRED STATE:

An IT Support Manager can open a reporting view, apply operational filters, review calculated SLA and ticket performance metrics, and export the exact filtered results for management review. All values are derived from approved lifecycle events and auditable history so decisions are based on trusted data.

KEY FUNCTIONALITY:

• Generate reporting metrics for first response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, backlog aging, and workload trends.

• Filter reports by reporting period, ticket category, priority, status, assignee, and organizational scope.

• Use ticket lifecycle timestamps, assignment history, and SLA metric records as the authoritative reporting sources.

• Present on-screen summaries and detailed rows that align with export output.

• Block unauthorized access to reporting and export functions.


USER INTERACTION FLOW:

1. The IT Support Manager opens the SLA performance and overdue reporting area from the support reporting interface.

2. The manager selects a reporting period and optional filters such as category, priority, status, assignee, and organizational scope.

3. The system validates the filter set, queries ticket lifecycle, assignment, and SLA metric data, and calculates the requested measures.

4. The system displays summary metrics and detailed report rows, including any count of excluded records caused by incomplete lifecycle data.

5. The manager adjusts filters to compare operational segments or reporting periods.

6. The manager exports the currently displayed report for review and record retention.


TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS:

• Data source: derive metrics from ticket records, controlled status transition timestamps, assignment audit history, and persisted SLA calculation data rather than free-text comments or non-audited fields.

• Validation: enforce valid date ranges, supported filter enumerations for status/priority/category, and assignee/organizational scope values that exist in the authorized dataset.

• Security: require authenticated access and role-based permission for report viewing and export; restrict dataset scope to the manager's authorized organizational visibility.

• Observability: log report execution time, filter payload, row counts, exclusion counts for incomplete timestamps, and export actions for troubleshooting and audit review.

• Performance: aggregate efficiently for common reporting periods and return results within acceptable dashboard/report response times even when filtering across large ticket volumes.


OUT OF SCOPE:

• Custom report builders or user-defined metric formulas.

• Editing ticket, SLA, category, or priority data from the reporting screen.

• Predictive analytics or staffing recommendations.


SUCCESS METRICS:

• Managers can generate and export filtered SLA performance reports without manual data preparation.

• Reported summary values reconcile with underlying lifecycle and SLA records for sampled periods.

• Report execution for standard date ranges completes within the operational response target for reporting screens.

Persona: IT Support Manager (IT Support Manager)

Design Prompt 

Unified interaction flow:
A ticket or SLA event occurs in the IT Help Desk system, such as ticket creation, assignment or reassignment, status update, comment, resolution, closure, SLA warning, SLA breach, escalation, or notification/reporting access.
The core ticket action is committed first, then a normalized notification or telemetry event is generated asynchronously so ticket processing is never blocked.
The notification orchestration layer evaluates event eligibility, recipient scope, role authorization, channel routing, sanitization, deduplication, and retry policy.
Employees receive only employee-safe lifecycle messages through confirmation, My Tickets, ticket detail, and status history touchpoints; agents receive operational assignment and activity signals; managers receive SLA risk and governance oversight signals; administrators and analysts access secure configuration, monitoring, and audit workflows.
Delivery outcomes such as SENT, FAILED, RETRIED, DENIED, and related states are recorded in immutable audit and telemetry history.
If access is unauthorized or delivery/configuration fails, the system preserves the committed source event, shows the correct denied or error state, and avoids leaking restricted ticket data, internal notes, attachment metadata, or secrets.

Figma Make instructions:

Create a web app system design for an IT Help Desk Management System focused only on notification-related experiences and the ticket lifecycle touchpoints that shape them.

Use a clean enterprise SaaS style:
- 1440px desktop frames
- neutral background
- blue primary actions
- semantic status colors
- compact data-dense layouts for ops/admin pages
- accessible spacing and strong hierarchy
- realistic top nav and left sidebar patterns

Global rules:
- Do not create any visible “User Journey” section in the UI
- Requester-facing screens must be sanitized and employee-safe
- Never expose internal comments, hidden notes, reassignment rationale for staff only, attachment internals, raw secrets, or restricted troubleshooting details on employee screens
- Monitoring and audit views are read-only unless the screen is explicitly configuration-related
- Show immutable audit concepts through labels, event history, timestamps, and references, not edit controls
- Unauthorized route states must be visually distinct from generic server errors
- Retry actions issue one new request and disable while in progress
- Preserve filters across drill-down, pagination, and return navigation on manager and ops screens

Create these pages:

Page 1: End User Notification Experiences
Build these frames:
1. Employee My Tickets
- top navigation with app name, notifications icon, profile menu
- lightweight left sidebar with My Tickets and New Ticket
- page title “My Tickets”
- filter chips for Status, Priority, Date Range
- table with columns: Ticket ID, Subject, Category, Priority, Current Status, Last Update, Notification Cue
- rows like TCK-2048, TCK-2055, T-1001
- show small status cues and safe notification indicators such as “Status updated”, “Resolved”, “Assigned”
- include pagination

2. Employee Ticket Detail
- breadcrumbs: My Tickets / TCK-2048
- ticket summary card with ticketId, category, priority, current status
- employee-safe timeline/history showing created, assigned, status updated, resolved, closed
- safe notification summary module with message preview cards for TICKET_CREATED, TICKET_ASSIGNED, TICKET_UPDATED, TICKET_RESOLVED, TICKET_CLOSED
- no internal agent notes
- include current status and timestamp labels

3. Ticket Created Success / Confirmation
- success panel with ticket reference, initial status, category, priority, created timestamp
- confirmation text that notification has been sent or queued
- CTA buttons: View Ticket, Back to My Tickets
- success toast variant visible

4. Unauthorized Ticket Access
- full-page access denied panel
- generic message without ticket details
- CTA: Return to My Tickets

5. No Tickets Empty State
- empty state panel with illustration placeholder
- text: “You have no support tickets yet”
- CTA: Create Ticket

Also include small state variants on this page:
- loading skeleton for My Tickets list
- validation error summary for invalid ticket lookup
- safe server error banner

Page 2: Agent and Manager Operational Notification Views
Build these frames:
1. Agent Ticket List
- top nav and left sidebar for agent workspace
- page title “Assigned Tickets”
- filter bar: Queue, Status, Priority, SLA State, Date Range
- table columns: Ticket ID, Subject, Assignee, Priority, Status, SLA State, Activity Indicator, Last Notification
- include assignment/activity icons for assignment, reassignment, comment, status change
- show denied-access row state pattern separately, not mixed with valid data
- include pagination

2. Agent Ticket Detail
- breadcrumbs: Assigned Tickets / TCK-2055
- header with ticket summary and assignment badge
- operational activity stream with assignment changes, comments, status changes, and notification states
- assignment history panel
- agent-targeted notification patterns for assignment, reassignment, comments, and status changes
- include visible status badges for Sent, Failed, Retried where notification outcomes are relevant
- include a denied-access state variant for out-of-scope ticket direct route

3. Reassignment Modal
- modal over agent detail
- assignee selector limited to eligible users only
- queue option if applicable
- inline eligibility validation
- confirm and cancel actions
- validation state if selected assignee is inactive or unauthorized
- disabled confirm while saving

4. Manager SLA / Notification Overview Dashboard
- KPI cards: At Risk, Breached, Overdue, Escalated, Active Notifications, Failed Deliveries
- cards for assignment/workload summaries

1. The system generates ticket performance reports for a selected reporting period showing response time, resolution time, SLA attainment percentage, backlog aging, and workload trend totals using ticket lifecycle timestamps and SLA calculation records.

2. An authorized IT Support Manager can filter report results by reporting period, ticket category, priority, status, assignee, and organizational scope, and the returned dataset reflects only records matching all selected filters.

3. Report calculations use only controlled ticket lifecycle states, assignment history, and auditable SLA metric data; tickets with incomplete required timestamps are excluded from time-based aggregates and counted in a visible data-quality exception total.

4. The system allows export of the filtered report in a supported file format and the exported rows and summary values match the report currently displayed on screen at the time of export.

5. If a user without reporting permission attempts to open or export SLA performance reporting, the system denies access and returns an authorization error without exposing ticket metrics or underlying ticket data.
